judged_text: `add_members` calls `usernames.split(",")` directly on `params.require(:usernames)` with no type coercion, so a request whose usernames param arrives as an array or hash (the natural JSON encoding for a list field) raises NoMethodError and returns a 500 instead of a 4xx. An admin API client sending {"usernames": ["alice","bob"]} — or any non-string value — to this newly introduced endpoint gets an unhandled NoMethodError (500 plus a stack trace in the error stream) rather than a validation error; `params[:usernames].to_s.split(",")` (or Array() wrapping) is the one-line fix. The shipped Ember client always sends a comma-joined string, so the defect is latent until any other consumer hits the endpoint.
